input: Write a personal development book review for my blog

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The specific book being reviewed determines everything — the themes to cover, claims to evaluate, and key takeaways to highlight.
Knowing who reads the blog shapes the language level, assumed knowledge, and which aspects of the book to emphasise.
Whether this is a standalone review or part of a series (e.g. a monthly book club feature) affects structure and framing.
A word count target or publish deadline directly constrains how deep and detailed the review can be.
The desired tone — critical and analytical vs. warm and encouraging — defines the voice and how honest critique is handled.
Understanding what the user wants readers to do after reading (buy the book, skip it, reflect on a lesson) shapes the review's conclusion and call to action.
Knowing the preferred format — summary, star rating, section headers, pull quotes — determines how the post is structured and delivered.

gold.taskTitle: Write a personal development book review for blog
gold.taskDescription: Write a blog post reviewing a personal development book, tailored to the user's audience, tone, and publishing goals.

questions.title: Which specific book are you reviewing?
questions.description: Identify the exact title and author of the personal development book to be reviewed, as this determines all content decisions.

questions.title: Who is the primary audience of your blog?
questions.description: Understand the reader profile — e.g. young professionals, entrepreneurs, general self-improvement seekers — to calibrate tone and depth.

questions.title: Is this a one-off review or part of a regular series?
questions.description: Determine whether the review needs to fit into a recurring format or template, such as a monthly book roundup or dedicated review column.

questions.title: What is your target word count or publish deadline?
questions.description: Establish any hard limits on length or timing that will constrain how thorough or detailed the review can be.

questions.title: Should the tone be critically analytical or warmly encouraging?
questions.description: Clarify the preferred voice — whether to give balanced critique including flaws, or to keep the review positive and motivational in style.

questions.title: What do you want readers to do after finishing the review?
questions.description: Define the intended reader outcome — e.g. buy the book, avoid it, apply one specific lesson — which drives the conclusion and call to action.

questions.title: What format should the review follow?
questions.description: Determine structural preferences such as use of section headers, a star rating, a summary box, pull quotes, or a free-flowing essay style.
